title: Functions
description: Functions, Result, closures, and deterministic cleanup in Rust
theory:
## Functions in Rust

Define functions with `fn`. Rust distinguishes statements and expressions; the last expression can be an implicit return.

### Multiple returns

Use `Result<T, E>` instead of `(T, error)` pairs.

### Closures

`|x| x + 1` captures environment; types are often inferred.

### Cleanup

Rust uses `Drop` and often `defer`-like patterns via guards; for simple ordering use an inner function or explicit calls. This chapter’s last exercise models “run last” with an inner closure.

exercises.title: Basic function
exercises.description: Define `fn greet()` printing `Hello` and call it from `main`.

exercises.title: Parameters
Return value
exercises.description: `add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32` return sum; print `add(3,4)`.
hints: `fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a + b }`

exercises.title: Result return
exercises.description: `divide(a,b) -> Result<i32,&'static str>` error on zero; print `Debug` of `(divide(10,3))`.

exercises.title: Variadic style
exercises.description: Implement `sum(nums: &[i32]) -> i32` summing slice; print sum of `[1,2,3,4,5]`.

exercises.title: Drop order demo
exercises.description: Print `start`, then `working`, then `end` using a helper that prints `end` when a guard struct drops.
hints: `Drop::drop` runs when `_end` goes out of scope after `working`.

exercises.title: Closure state
exercises.description: Implement `make_adder` returning `impl FnMut(i32) -> i32`; print results of `5` then `10` cumulative.
hints: `let mut sum = 0; move |x| { sum += x; sum }`
